declarations.name: euler_firewall_separation
declarations.doc: The pre-spectral firewall, as a separation.** For every genuine (multiplicative) Dirichlet coefficient function `f`, the Bohr lift factors over the primes at every `n`; yet the Davenport–Heilbronn-style fake coefficient fails that factorization at some finite `n`. The Euler product / Bohr factorization property separates the genuine from the fake, pre-spectrally — no zero is examined.

declarations.name: exists_prime_tilt_sign_pair
declarations.doc: The torus quadrant supply for the two basepoint tilts.** At the two basepoints `ρ ± c·i` of a narrow annulus in the strip, the two orientation-steering tilt increments realize EVERY sign pair at every prime scale: the pair `(primeTilt q (1−conj(ρ+ci)), primeTilt q (1−conj(ρ−ci)))` visits all four quadrants. This two-frequency steering is the structure that requires the Euler product — the walk's support IS the primes — and is what a Davenport–Heilbronn analogue lacks.

declarations.name: kneser_core
declarations.doc: DeVos's argument.** When the stabiliser of `A * B` is trivial and `A ∩ B` is a nonempty proper subset of `A`, the Cauchy--Davenport bound `#A + #B ≤ #(A * B) + 1` holds.

### 10.2 The Davenport–Heilbronn function is a counterexample `[FALSIFIES §7]`

Take the modulus `Q = 5`, `chi` the quartic character with `chi(2) = i`. The odd functions on
`Z/5` supported on the units are spanned by `chi` and `chi-bar`, so every FE eigenvector of that
parity is `alpha = (1, xi, -xi, -1, 0)` on residues `(1,2,3,4,0)` for a real `xi`, with
`alpha = c_1 chi + c_3 chi-bar`, `c_1 = (1 - i xi)/2`, `c_3 = (1 + i xi)/2`.

The eigenvector equations `-c_3 \bar u = eps c_1`, `c_1 u = eps c_3` with `u = tau(chi)/sqrt5` give
`eps^2 = -1`, i.e. `eps = ± i`, and

  `(1 - i xi)/(1 + i xi) = eps / u`,  hence  `xi = -tan(phi/2)`,  `e^{i phi} = eps / u`.

Both signs of `eps` occur. Replacing `eps` by `-eps` sends `phi` to `phi + pi` and hence
`xi = -tan(phi/2)` to `-1/xi`: the two resulting functions are the two Davenport–Heilbronn functions
with opposite root numbers, and their parameters are **reciprocal**, `xi' = -1/xi`.

Two exact facts are all that is needed, and no numerics enter.

- **`|xi| ≠ 1`.** `|xi| = |tan(phi/2)| = 1` iff `phi ≡ ± pi/2 (mod 2 pi)`, iff `e^{i phi} = ± i`,
  iff `eps/u = ± i`, iff `u = ± 1` (as `eps = ± i`), iff the Gauss sum `tau(chi)` is real. But
  `tau(chi) = sum_{n=1}^{4} chi(n) e(n/5) = -2 sin(4 pi/5) + 2 i sin(2 pi/5)` has imaginary part
  `2 sin(2 pi/5) ≠ 0`. So `|xi| ≠ 1`.
- **Exactly one branch has `|xi| > 1`**, since the two parameters are `xi` and `-1/xi` and
  `|xi| ≠ 1`.

Also `xi` is real (`phi` is real), and `alpha` is not multiplicative: `alpha(2)^2 = xi^2 >= 0` while
`alpha(4) = -1`. By Saias–Weingartner both branches therefore have infinitely many zeros with
`sigma > 1`.

## §16 The additivity conjecture is RETRACTED — tested and falsified

§15 conjectured that no RH proof can come from a criterion in which the functional equation and the
Euler product appear as separate additive terms.  I tested it two ways.  It fails both.

**Test 1 — the classification.**  Kaczorowski–Perelli (*On the structure of the Selberg class, I:
0 ≤ d ≤ 1*, Acta Math. 182 (1999)) classify the degree-one elements of the Selberg class: they are
exactly `zeta` and the shifted Dirichlet `L`-functions.  So the *joint* hypothesis — functional
equation with Gamma-factor, Euler product, Ramanujan bound, degree one — **has no counterexample
family at all.**  There is no "Davenport–Heilbronn with an Euler product" and no
"Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer with a Gamma-factor functional equation": the two no-go families of §14
and §15 cannot be merged.  Consequently the joint input is *not* known to be insufficient, and an
argument may legitimately consume it additively.

**Test 2 — my own artifacts.**  Apply the filter to the ladders built this month.  They use
`Lambda >= 0` on the prime side (so they do **not** apply to Davenport–Heilbronn, whose logarithmic
derivative has no nonnegative Dirichlet expansion) and the functional-equation Klein involution on
the divisor side (so they do **not** apply to a Beurling system, which has no such symmetry).  They
are additive criteria that nonetheless consume both inputs essentially.  So "additive implies dead"
is false, and my own work is the counterexample.

> **[RETRACTED]**  the additivity obstruction of §15.  What blocks the ladders is the resolution law
> of §8, not the additive shape of the explicit formula.

Third self-correction of this investigation, and the most useful one: it removes a conclusion that
would have wrongly condemned a large part of the corpus.

## §17 What survives: a two-sided filter, and the triage it gives

The durable residue of §§14–16 is not an obstruction but a **test every proposed argument must
pass**, in both directions:

> **[FILTER]**  An argument for RH must fail when applied to Davenport–Heilbronn — hence it must use
> the coefficients' positivity or multiplicativity, not merely the functional equation and the
> Dirichlet-series support.  And it must fail when applied to a Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer Beurling
> system — hence it must use the Gamma-factor functional equation, not merely an Euler product with
> `Lambda >= 0`.  An argument that survives *either* substitution proves too much and is dead.

| corpus family | uses | filter verdict |

| 3-4-1, von Mangoldt moment arrays, prime-trace positive-definiteness | `Lambda >= 0` only | survives DMVZ substitution ⇒ **cannot close alone** |
| Herglotz, vertical monotonicity, Hankel/Grommer, Li, screw, Weil involution | FE + divisor structure only | survive DH substitution ⇒ sound as *criteria*, dead as *proof routes* unless coefficient information is injected |

The middle row is the largest class in this corpus and the verdict on it is sharp: those cards are

The corpus already carries Davenport–Heilbronn and Beurling material in backlog

## Goal

Give the Davenport-Heilbronn gate a concrete shifted-square-test form. Functional-equation symmetry can force the quartet pattern, but it does not imply shifted Stieltjes positivity: an off-line quartet is detected by the first nontrivial shifted Hankel minors.

## Proof

[PROVED HERE]

Work in seam coordinates `w=s-1/2` and reciprocal coordinate

```text
y = -1/w^2.
```

An FE-symmetric, real-conjugation-symmetric off-line quartet has points

```text
w in { a+i gamma, -a+i gamma, a-i gamma, -a-i gamma },
```

with `a>0` and `gamma>0`. Define

```text
T_k = sum_{quartet} y^k.
```

Direct algebra gives

```text
det [[T_1,T_2],[T_2,T_3]]
  = -64 a^2 gamma^2 / (a^2+gamma^2)^6,
```

and

```text
det [[T_2,T_3],[T_3,T_4]]
  = -64 a^2 gamma^2 / (a^2+gamma^2)^8.
```

Both determinants are strictly negative when `a gamma != 0`. Therefore the degree-one shifted blocks

```text
H_1^(0) = [T_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^1,
H_1^(1) = [T_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^1
```

are not PSD for an off-line quartet.

At `a=0`, the quartet collapses to duplicated on-line conjugate points. Then `y=1/gamma^2` is positive and the same determinants vanish, giving the expected rank-one PSD boundary case.

/-- **The field's First Theorem (Euler product ⟺ Bohr-lift factorization).**
A Dirichlet coefficient function `f` is multiplicative (has an Euler product) iff it is
normalized `f 1 = 1` and its Bohr lift factors over the prime coordinates, i.e.
`f n = ∏_{p ∣ n} f (p ^ vₚ(n))` for every `n ≠ 0`. -/
@[aesop norm simp]
theorem isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ) :
    f.IsMultiplicative ↔
      (f 1 = 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → f n = n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k)) := by
  constructor
  · intro hf
    exact ⟨hf.map_one, fun n hn =>
      ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.multiplicative_factorization f hf hn⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, hfact⟩
    rw [ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.iff_ne_zero]
    refine ⟨h1, ?_⟩
    intro m n hm hn hcop
    have hdisj : Disjoint m.factorization.support n.factorization.support := by
      rw [Nat.support_factorization, Nat.support_factorization]
      exact hcop.disjoint_primeFactors
    rw [hfact (m * n) (Nat.mul_ne_zero hm hn), hfact m hm, hfact n hn,
        Nat.factorization_mul hm hn, Finsupp.prod_add_index_of_disjoint hdisj]

/-- **The pre-spectral firewall.** A normalized (`f 1 = 1`) Dirichlet series with **no
Euler product** (non-multiplicative `f`) fails the prime factorization at some finite `n`:
there is `n ≠ 0` with `f n ≠ ∏_{p ∣ n} f (p ^ vₚ(n))`. The failure of the Euler product is
witnessed at a finite `n`, before any zero is examined — the fake-family obstruction made
intrinsic and pre-spectral. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem fake_fails_factorization (f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ)
    (h1 : f 1 = 1) (hnm : ¬ f.IsMultiplicative) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 ∧ f n ≠ n.factorization.prod fun p k => f (p ^ k) := by
  by_contra h
  push Not at h
  exact hnm ((isMultiplicative_iff_bohr_factorization f).mpr ⟨h1, h⟩)

/-- The real part of the primitive order-4 Dirichlet character modulo `5`, as used
in the Davenport-Heilbronn-style fake-family witness: residues `1,4` have real
parts `1,-1`, and residues `0,2,3` have real part `0`. -/
def davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  match n % 5 with
  | 1 => 1
  | 4 => -1
  | _ => 0

/-- The corresponding normalized arithmetic-function coefficient model over `ℂ`.
This is only the finite coefficient firewall witness, not a formalization of the
Davenport-Heilbronn function, its functional equation, or its zeros. -/
def davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff : ArithmeticFunction ℂ :=
  ZeroHom.mk (fun n => (davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt n : ℂ)) (by
    norm_num [davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeffInt])

/-- **Concrete fake-family firewall witness.** The mod-5 Davenport-Heilbronn-style
coefficient model is not multiplicative: `a_6 = 1` but `a_2 a_3 = 0`. This is the
finite, pre-spectral obstruction behind the chat computation; it examines no zeros
and proves no RH/GRH localization statement. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff_not_isMultiplicative :
    ¬ davenportHeilbronnFakeCoeff.IsMultiplicative := by
  intro hmul

/-!
# The Cauchy-Davenport theorem

This file proves a generalisation of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem to arbitrary groups.

Cauchy-Davenport provides a lower bound on the size of `s + t` in terms of the sizes of `s` and `t`,
where `s` and `t` are nonempty finite sets in a monoid. Precisely, it says that
`|s + t| ≥ |s| + |t| - 1` unless the RHS is bigger than the size of the smallest nontrivial subgroup
(in which case taking `s` and `t` to be that subgroup would yield a counterexample). The motivating
example is `s = {0, ..., m}`, `t = {0, ..., n}` in the integers, which gives
`s + t = {0, ..., m + n}` and `|s + t| = m + n + 1 = |s| + |t| - 1`.

There are two kinds of proof of Cauchy-Davenport:
* The first one works in linear orders by writing `a₁ < ... < aₖ` the elements of `s`,
  `b₁ < ... < bₗ` the elements of `t`, and arguing that `a₁ + b₁ < ... < aₖ + b₁ < ... < aₖ + bₗ`
  are distinct elements of `s + t`.
* The second one works in groups by performing an "e-transform". In an abelian group, the
  e-transform replaces `s` and `t` by `s ∩ g • s` and `t ∪ g⁻¹ • t`. For a suitably chosen `g`, this
  decreases `|s + t|` and keeps `|s| + |t|` the same. In a general group, we use a trickier
  e-transform (in fact, a pair of e-transforms), but the idea is the same.

## Main declarations

* `cauchy_davenport_minOrder_mul`: A generalisation of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem to arbitrary
  groups.
* `cauchy_davenport_of_isTorsionFree`: The Cauchy-Davenport theorem in torsion-free groups.
* `ZMod.cauchy_davenport`: The Cauchy-Davenport theorem for `ZMod p`.
* `cauchy_davenport_mul_of_linearOrder_isCancelMul`: The Cauchy-Davenport theorem in linear ordered
  cancellative semigroups.

## TODO

Version for `circle`.

## References

* Matt DeVos, *On a generalization of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem*

## Tags

additive combinatorics, number theory, sumset, cauchy-davenport
-/

    Nat.cast_le] at *

      ih _ _ ht.inv hs.inv
